content.user_title: Build Python Test Suites with pytest
content.value_statement: Python teams need repeatable patterns for unit, integration, async, database, and CI tests. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pytest examples and testing workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains pytest test structure with arrange, act, and assert patterns.
Shows fixture setup, teardown, scope, autouse fixtures, and conftest organization.
Demonstrates mocking for HTTP clients, exceptions, and external dependencies.
Covers parameterized tests, async tests, temporary files, and database sessions.
Provides coverage commands, pytest configuration examples, and CI workflow guidance.
Introduces property-based testing with Hypothesis strategies.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a test runner.
It cannot verify project results without running the project test suite.
Example API, database, and key values are placeholders for adaptation.
Project-specific fixtures and CI settings still require local review.

use_cases.title: Start a pytest suite
use_cases.description: Create focused unit tests, fixtures, and naming conventions for a new Python package.

use_cases.title: Improve service testing
use_cases.description: Mock HTTP clients, isolate database tests, and add coverage checks for a Python service.

use_cases.title: Standardize team practices
use_cases.description: Define test organization, markers, CI commands, and review expectations for a shared repository.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to design pytest tests for this function. Include clear test names, edge cases, and expected failures.

prompt_templates.title: Add fixtures and mocks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to refactor these tests with fixtures and mocks. Keep external services isolated and explain the fixture scope choices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan integration coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to build a test plan for this Python service. Include unit, integration, async, database, and coverage checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI testing strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-testing-patterns to define a CI testing strategy for this repository. Include markers, coverage thresholds, matrix choices, and failure triage.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to test a new calculator module.
output_examples.output: A pytest plan with basic unit cases, edge cases, descriptive test names, and exception scenarios.

output_examples.input: A service test suite calls external APIs during tests.
output_examples.output: A mock-based testing approach that isolates HTTP calls, checks expected requests, and handles error responses.

output_examples.input: A team wants better CI confidence for a Python package.
output_examples.output: A test organization plan with markers, coverage reporting, Python version matrix guidance, and review practices.

best_practices: Keep tests independent, deterministic, and clear about the behavior under test.
Use fixtures and mocks to isolate external systems and reduce repeated setup.
Measure coverage, but prioritize meaningful assertions and important failure paths.
anti_patterns: Do not let tests depend on real network services unless they are explicit integration tests.
Do not hide broad setup inside unclear fixtures that make failures hard to diagnose.
Do not chase coverage percentages while leaving critical behavior unasserted.

faq.question: Does this skill write tests for an existing project?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and prompts that help Claude, Codex, or Claude Code draft tests for project code.

faq.question: Does it require pytest?
faq.answer: The examples focus on pytest, with related coverage, mocking, async, and Hypothesis tools.

faq.question: Can it help with integration tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for API clients, database sessions, markers, and CI workflows.

faq.question: Can it run the tests?
faq.answer: No. It is a guidance skill. The connected agent or developer must run commands in the project environment.

faq.question: Are the API and database values real?
faq.answer: No. They are placeholders used to explain testing techniques and should be replaced in real projects.

faq.question: Is it useful for test-driven development?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to write focused tests around expected behavior before or alongside implementation.
